LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices for a VCS-based package. The `source` array fetches the project's own upstream repository (`git+https://github.com/hyprwm/aquamarine.git`) using a standard git+ URL. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is expected and required for VCS sources—it is not a security issue for this audit gate. The `pkgver()` function only executes local git commands (`git tag`, `git describe`, `git rev-list`, `git rev-parse`) on the freshly cloned repository to generate a version string based on tags and commits. There are no network requests to unexpected hosts, no obfuscated code, no `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, or `wget` calls, and no file operations beyond what `makepkg` itself performs to clone and extract the source.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR git package, safe for source fetch and pkgver</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard AUR -git package for the aquamarine library from the official Hyprland GitHub organization. It declares dependencies and build dependencies appropriate for a Wayland rendering backend. The source is fetched via git from the project's own upstream repository (https://github.com/hyprwm/aquamarine), and the sha256sums is correctly set to 'SKIP' as required for VCS sources. The pkgver() function computes the version from local git tags and history without any external network calls. The build() and package() functions use cmake/ninja in a standard out-of-tree build and install into $pkgdir via DESTDIR. No suspicious commands (curl, wget, eval, base64), obfuscation, data exfiltration, or unexpected file operations are present. The file follows conventional AUR packaging practices throughout.
</details>
